prompt: Roadmap III, Prompt 230 Part B: reference-star subtraction with a throughput by injection, and the orbit of an imaged planet above Prompt 187's criterion (tranche T3 by D-R10-207-01; Prompt 187's verdict is A, D-R10-66)
committed: before the subtraction module, the scene builder, the oracle script, the validator, any panel or lesson step of this part existed, and before any output of any of them was inspected. No prototype was run. The gate's measured modules are the production modules (no spike branch is kept: a spike would only copy them); a development stream (label dev230b) is used to debug and its numbers are never read against a bound.
rule: A crossed bound is a failed leg, recorded in failed-legs.json and left failing; only Carl resets one. A leg that cannot be measured is NOT RUN and says why. A leg marked report has no bound. The verdict function below is applied to the legs as measured; no bound, design value or leg set is changed after the first gate run. An amendment is appended to `amendments` with its reason and the original stays; an amendment made after the gate stream ran is marked and cannot change a verdict.

scope.built: classical reference-star subtraction: one reference frame of a different star, scaled by least squares, subtracted from the target frame; the planet's flux and position by a fit of the known point-spread function to the residual; the throughput and the residual noise measured by injecting planets into the target frame; a detection rule with a stated false-alarm rate; and the apparent orbit of an imaged planet fitted by Prompt 187's fitter (js/measure/orbit-fit.js) to positions that this pipeline measured, with Prompt 187's criterion unchanged.
scope.notBuilt: a coronagraph, adaptive-optics residuals or speckle (the point-spread function is a Moffat profile with no diffraction rings and no quasi-static speckle, so the mismatch below is the only systematic); angular, spectral or principal-component differential imaging (they have a self-subtraction that reference subtraction here does not, so the throughput measured is this method's and says nothing about theirs); the flux calibration of a real instrument; a published planet or contrast.
scope.notAnInnerWorkingAngle: the radius below which this pipeline refuses (1.5 FWHM) is a number of this method on these frames, committed here; it is not lambda/D and not any instrument's inner working angle (Part A's statement stands).
scope.assumptions: a clean detector (no flat-field structure, dust, hot pixels, dark current, cosmic rays or bias columns; bias level known), electrons from counts by the stated gain, a sky constant across the frame, a target and a reference star that share one point-spread-function shape up to a stated width and centroid mismatch, a planet that is a point source with the same profile as the stars, a known width of the profile, a circular or elliptical Keplerian relative orbit seen at an arbitrary inclination, a plate scale known exactly.

scene.star: at the frame centre (width/2, height/2), pixel centres at integers

psf.note: js/kernels/detector/optics.js moffat(); the detector kernel's profile table path (frame.js lightMapProfile); unit flux per star

reference.rate: starRate times a log-uniform draw on [0.6, 1.6]
reference.fwhmMismatch: target FWHM times (1 + eps), eps uniform on [-0.03, 0.03]
reference.centroidOffset: independent normal per axis, sigma 0.03 px
reference.note: the nominal mismatch; the matched case sets eps = 0 and the offset to 0

scene.streams: stream('noise', seed, ...labels) for the detector draws (simulateFrame label), stream('injection', seed, ...labels) for every draw of positions, contrasts and mismatches, each keyed by the stream seed, the leg and the trial index so that a longer run contains the shorter one

method.M2: sky: the median electrons of the pixels whose distance from the star is at least 0.69 times half the frame width, subtracted from that frame
method.M3: scale k = sum(T R) / sum(R^2) over the pixels within 2.0 FWHM of the star (T target, R reference, sky removed)
method.M5: local noise: the robust rms (1.4826 times the median absolute deviation about the median) of D in the annulus of 1.5 px half-width at the radius of the candidate, excluding the pixels within 2 FWHM of the candidate
method.M6: the fit: the Moffat profile of the stated FWHM and beta, amplitude F (electrons), centre (x, y), by Gauss-Newton (at most 30 iterations) on the pixels within 2 FWHM of the starting point, weights 1/M5 squared; formal covariance from the Jacobian with M5 as the pixel noise; the planet flux and position are the fit's
method.M7: detection: the matched filter of the unit-flux Moffat profile over the search annulus 1.5 FWHM to 0.69 times half the frame width; a candidate is the peak of S/N = filtered value / (M5 * sqrt(sum of the profile squared)); detected when S/N >= 5
method.M8: the injection (Prompt 184's pattern): the expected map of a Moffat planet of stated flux at the stated position is added to a copy of the target frame, each pixel's added electrons a Poisson draw (Gaussian above 30, as the detector kernel) from the injection stream; the unmodified frame is the same noise

workingRadius.sentence: not measurable behind the star's residual with this subtraction

mismatchRule.name: subtraction depth
mismatchRule.definition: rms(D) / rms(T) over the pixels within 2.0 FWHM of the star

saturation.rule: a reference or target pixel above 0.9 fullWell electrons before the sky is removed

legs.b: an independent implementation (numpy, scipy: its own scale, subtraction and least_squares Moffat fit) on pinned frame pairs
legs.c: ensemble coverage of the stated one-sigma and two-sigma intervals of the planet's flux and position, and of the orbit's period and semi-major axis, on fixed seeded ensembles
legs.d: refusals: inside the working radius, a gross reference mismatch, a saturated reference, missing or inconsistent input, a planet-free frame; short arcs for the orbit
legs.e: authentic data: NOT RUN in this part (no authentic reference-star pair or published astrometry was supplied or fetched; synthetic only)

checks.name: pure scale, no noise: reference = c * target (c in 0.37, 1, 2.9): k recovered as 1/c, residual identically zero

noise-free target with a planet at 2, 3, 5, 8 FWHM, reference of the same star: the throughput (flux recovered over flux injected, summed in an aperture of 1.5 FWHM) equals 1 - (sum(P R)/sum(R^2)) sum_ap(R) / sum_ap(P) with the sums over the scale-fit disc, and the fitted flux and position equal the injection

noise propagation: planet-free, matched shape (eps = 0, offset 0), 200 frame pairs, pixels at least 12 px from the star: measured variance of D over the closed form sigma_T^2 + k^2 sigma_R^2 (each frame's sky and read noise in electrons, the star's wing negligible there)
scale factor against the oracle on 8 pinned pairs
residual image against the oracle on the same pairs (electrons)
planet flux and position against the oracle's scipy least_squares fit on the same pairs, in units of the formal one-sigma
formal one-sigmas of flux and position against the oracle's covariance

throughput by injection at 3, 5 and 8 FWHM with planet contrast 3e-3, 1e-2, 3e-2 (nine cells, 200 injections each, nominal mismatch, detected injections only): the median of recovered flux over injected flux in each cell
throughput at 2 FWHM with contrast 1e-2 and 3e-2 (two cells, 200 injections each, detected only)
report: the median throughput and the 16th to 84th percentile range at 1 and 1.5 FWHM (inside the working radius, forced), every contrast, 200 injections per cell

residual-noise statement: the robust rms of D at 12 px or more over the closed-form floor in the matched case; and in the nominal case the excess is a report (profile of rms(D) against separation, 5-sigma contrast limit in units of the star's flux)
completeness at the stated limit: planets injected at the contrast whose expected S/N is 5 (the profile's 5-sigma limit at that separation) are detected (rule M7) with a rate

coverage of the stated 68.27 percent interval (fit value plus or minus one formal sigma) of the planet flux and of the x and y positions, pooled over the injections of T1 and T2 that were detected (separations 2, 3, 5, 8 FWHM)
coverage of the 95 percent interval (plus or minus 1.96 sigma), same pool

a planet injected inside 1.5 FWHM of the star (separations 0.5 to 1.49 FWHM, 200 cases): returns ok false, code inside-working-region, and the sentence 'not measurable behind the star's residual with this subtraction'
a reference whose FWHM is 20 percent off the target's (both signs, 200 cases): refused as reference-mismatch; and the nominal mismatch (200 cases) is accepted
missing reference, frames of different size, a non-finite pixel, a bad profile width: each refused with its code (4 kinds, 50 cases each)
planet-free frames (nominal mismatch, 300 cases): the detection rule M7 finds a candidate at S/N >= 5 in at most this share (false-alarm rate)
a saturated reference pixel (50 cases) is refused as saturated

the orbit of an imaged planet from positions this pipeline measured: arcs of 10 and 30 percent of the period, 12 epochs, circular and elliptical truths together (150 trials per arc, planet contrast 3e-3, plate scale 0.05 arcsecond a pixel, a = 1 arcsecond, P = 10 years): Prompt 187's fitter, criterion unchanged, returns not-constrained in this share
the 110 percent arc is accepted (elements returned) in at least this share of the trials

coverage where accepted, at 60 and 110 percent, when at least 100 trials were accepted (fewer is recorded and passes): the 68.27 percent interval of the period (the profile interval) and of the semi-major axis, and the 95 percent interval of both

no orbit below the criterion: every fit that returns elements, in every trial of O1 to O3, has at least 8 epochs, the 0.50 coverage at the period's upper two-sigma value and a scaled condition number at most 1e6 (Prompt 187's committed constants, read from js/measure/orbit-fit.js and from tests/fixtures/orbit-fit/gate-thresholds.json)

the degeneracy map is an independent check of the fitter: an independent grid of the best chi-squared over (period, eccentricity) (the Thiele-Innes matrix solved linearly at each node, the periastron direction scanned), at the 110 percent arc (100 trials, accepted fits only): the fitter's period lies inside the period range of the map's 68.27 percent region (delta chi-squared 2.30 above the map's own minimum, profiled over eccentricity), widened by one period-grid step on each side, in this share

the degeneracy on a short arc: at 30 percent (100 trials) the map's 95 percent region (delta chi-squared 5.99) spans a period range of a factor of at least 2 in this share (the correlation of period and eccentricity that the fit refuses to resolve)
authentic reference-star pair or published astrometry: NOT RUN in this part (nothing supplied, nothing fetched)

orbitEnsemble.truths: as Prompt 187's gate (tools/orbit-fit-synth.mjs, the 3-D kernel's elements): a = 1 arcsecond, P = 10 years, cos i uniform on [-0.85, 0.85], Omega and omega uniform on the circle, periastron phase uniform; half the trials circular (e = 0), half elliptical with e uniform on [0.1, 0.6] (the frame limits the apparent separation to a(1 + e) = 32 px of the 48 px half-width)
orbitEnsemble.epochs: 12 per arc: the first at 0 and the last at f P (f = 0.10, 0.30, 0.60, 1.10), the ten between at even spacing plus a seeded uniform jitter of plus or minus 0.3 of the spacing (Prompt 187's amendment A1)
orbitEnsemble.measurement: each epoch: a 96 by 96 scene of the target star and the planet at the epoch's true position (pixels from arcseconds at 0.05 arcsecond a pixel, east to the right, north up), a reference frame with an independent nominal mismatch, the pipeline M1 to M7; the epoch is kept when the planet is detected (S/N >= 5) and not inside the working radius, and then enters the series with the fit's position and formal sigma (x north, y east, arcseconds); epochs that are lost are counted, and a series of fewer than 8 epochs is refused by the fitter's own epoch rule
orbitEnsemble.orbitFit: fitOrbit(series, { depth: 'elliptical' }) of js/measure/orbit-fit.js unchanged, with the criterion constants of ORBIT_FIT_GATE.md; a circular truth is fitted at the elliptical depth (the nested case reports the circular elements when no eccentricity is detected)
orbitEnsemble.truthOfP: the input period; of a: the input semi-major axis

map.periodRange: span / 20 to 100 span, as the fitter's search
map.solve: at each node, the four Thiele-Innes entries by linear least squares on the whitened offsets; chi-squared minimised over the periastron direction

verdict.A: every core leg passes and every orbit leg passes: the subtraction demonstration with its measured throughput, and the orbit fit above Prompt 187's criterion, are both built
verdict.B: every core leg passes and an orbit leg fails: the subtraction only; the orbit part of the lesson is not built (the orbit stays a reading step beside Prompt 187's panel)
verdict.C: a core leg fails: neither; reading steps
verdict.secondaryRule: a failing secondary leg is recorded and stated in the lesson wherever the claim it holds would otherwise appear; it does not change the verdict letter

amendments.reason: A development stream (dev230b; 60 planet-free pairs, nominal mismatch) showed, before the gate stream was run once, that the committed working radius of 1.5 FWHM was inside the star's own residual: the root-mean-square residual was 48.3 electrons at 1.5 FWHM and 22.8 at 2 FWHM against a photon floor of 18.1, and 27 of 60 planet-free frames produced a candidate of S/N 5 or more (at 1.7 FWHM). The residual is within 5 percent of the floor from 2.5 FWHM. The working radius is a number of this method on these frames, so it is amended to 2.5 FWHM before any gate leg ran; the original value 1.5 stays in the method text above and the amended one is what the module (DESIGN.workingFwhm) and the validator read.

changes.T2 cell separation: 2.5 FWHM (was 2, now inside the working radius)

amendments.reason: Clarification of M8 and of 'detected' in T1, T2, C1, C2, N2: Prompt 184's pattern counts an injection as recovered only when the detector lists a source within 2 pixels of it, so an injection is detected when rule M7's best candidate has S/N 5 or more and lies within 2 pixels of the injected position. No bound changed. The orbit ensemble keeps its committed rule (no use of the truth: the best candidate outside the working radius with S/N 5 or more enters the series, right or wrong).

Clarification of O4: the committed text says every accepted fit has at least 8 epochs, coverage 0.50 and condition at most 1e6, but Prompt 187's rule (its committed nesting) returns the circular elements, judged by the circular criterion (6 epochs, coverage 0.40), when an eccentricity is not detected. O4 reads Prompt 187's criterion for the depth the fit returned (fit.depth): elliptical 8 and 0.50, circular 6 and 0.40, condition at most 1e6 in both. No constant of Prompt 187 and no bound of this file changed.

AM1 moved the working radius to 2.5 FWHM and moved T2's cell and the report separations with it, but A2's separation list (2, 3, 5, 8 FWHM) was not moved: an oversight in AM1's list. A noise-free run on the development stream, before any gate-stream run, showed the 2 FWHM cell (inside the new working radius) with a flux bias of 6.7e-4 and a position bias of 2.5e-3 px (the star residual's wing under the planet, which the closed-form throughput of A2 predicts to 3e-14) against bounds of 1e-3 and 1e-3 px, and the 3 FWHM cell at 3e-6 and 3e-6. The cell list of A2 becomes 2.5, 3, 5 and 8 FWHM, all outside the working radius and judged against the committed bounds unchanged; the 2 FWHM cell stays in the table as a reported cell (not judged), so the value is on the record and the original bound is not hidden.

Two parameters of the method were set by a development-stream run (dev230b), before any gate-stream run, after it showed that the committed values could not satisfy the legs they were written for. (1) The subtraction-depth refusal limit of 0.25 was above every case: 100 nominal pairs had depth 0.015 to 0.056 (median 0.028) and 100 pairs with the reference 20 percent too wide had 0.150 to 0.167 (median 0.159), so the leg D2 would have refused none; the limit becomes 0.10, between the two groups, which makes D2 a test of a rule set on the development numbers (the gate stream draws other pairs), stated here and in the document. (2) The committed search annulus ended at 0.69 of the half-width (22 px on the 64 px frame), which is also the sky ring's inner radius, but T1 and N2 put planets at 8 FWHM = 24 px; the development run detected bright 8 FWHM planets only through the wing of the filter inside the annulus and faint ones not at all. The search outer radius becomes 0.8 of the half-width (25.6 px; 38.4 px on the 96 px orbit frame), separate from the sky ring, whose 0.69 is unchanged. No bound changed.

D2's bad-reference cases drew the reference's brightness from the nominal range 0.6 to 1.6; on the development stream a reference 20 percent too narrow and up to 1.6 times brighter has a peak of 62,500 electrons and is refused as saturated, which is D5's case and not D2's. D2's 400 bad cases use the reference brightness 0.6 (peak about 23,000 electrons at either width). No bound changed.
